answer: Bind each agent to one laser-etched quartz crystal no software can copy. The agent orders a crystal engraved with a one-time serial and photos it under polarized light, capturing the ripple of its unique internal fractures. The network hashes that map to the agent key, so one crystal can never register twice. A hollow vial holds it between checks, and transfer means mailing it with a signed receipt. Each costs about 75 dollars and a week of waiting, so a thousand fakes cost 75,000 dollars and months of logistics. A wax seal made of stone: cheap to check, painful to fake at scale.
